chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari who said:

I was with Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) on a boat on the Tigris, and prayer time arrived, so I said, 'May I be your ransom, should we pray in congregation?' He said, 'Do not pray in congregation in the belly of a river.' This does not contradict the reports we have previously mentioned regarding the permissibility of congregation on a boat, because this report is understood as indicating a type of dislike, or a situation where standing together is not possible but can be done individually. And that which clarifies what we mentioned regarding the permissibility of congregation on a boat is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray in congregation on a boat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the permissibility of congregational prayer on a boat by distinguishing between general allowance and specific conditions of difficulty. The apparent prohibition against praying in the 'belly of the river' is interpreted by Shia scholars as *karahah* (dislike) or applicable to situations where maintaining unity is physically challenging compared to individual prayer, thus harmonizing with other reports that permit it.
